headline: Committee discussed e-moto and e-bike safety rules but took no formal action on ordinance changes.
summary: The committee heard public comments on e-bike and e-moto safety, education, and enforcement, then discussed possible ordinance changes with input from Parks and Recreation and DPW staff. Members agreed to write up individual and collective recommendations for a future meeting and asked the Mayor to consider appointing a coordinator for a citywide educational campaign. The committee plans to meet again on September 17 and circulate its lists by September 2.

Ordinance Committee 
Thursday, August 20, 2026 
Bushor Conference Room, City Hall 
or Remote via Zoom. Burlington, Vermont 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 
 
Members Present: Councilor Bergman (Chair), Councilor Barlow, Councilor Carpenter (on-
line) 
Staff Present: Kim Sturtevant (Assistant City Attorney), Laura Wheelock (City Engineer), Phil 
Lewis (Director of Parks and Recreation) 
Public Present: Sharon Bushor, Richard Hillyard, Polly Vanderputten (public and school board 
member), Councilor Melo Grant 
Meeting called to order at 4:34 PM. 
1. Adopt the Agenda 
1.1 Adopt the Agenda 
Motion to Adopt Agenda. 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter. 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
2. Adopt Draft Minutes 
2.1 Adopt Draft Minutes from July 16, 2026 
Motion to Adopt minutes. 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter. 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
Councilor Bergman noted the minutes for the Joint Planning Commission and Ordinance 
Committee’s IZ work would be adopted at the next meeting.   
 
3. Public Forum 
Richard Hillyard of Ward 1 advocated for more education in every city and school regarding e-
scooter and e-bike safety, emphasizing resources need to be multilingual, as from their 
perspective, many cyclists in general do not obey road rules.     
Polly Vanderputten of Ward 2 commented that riding behavior for e-bikes and e-motos seems to 
be different from bicycles, so road rules need to be clarified, and the public and students need to
be educated on those rules.  Vanderputten also noted that drivers need to be more educated on 
how to share the road with cyclists.   
Sharon Bushor commented from a pedestrian perspective that traffic laws for bikes are 
confusing, and riding behavior is too inconsistent to know what to expect when sharing the road.  
Bushor stated education needs to target walkers, bikers, and vehicle drivers, that enforcement 
needs to be part of the strategy, and that the whole community needs to urgently band together 
on this issue.  Bushor also added that other traffic rules should be reconsidered, such as the age 
limit for riding on sidewalks.      
Public Forum closed at 4:52 PM.  
4.  Motorized Bicycle Ordinance Discussion 
Councilor Barlow commented that while enforcement was important, education was key and the 
school will need to take an active role in that, including in educating parents, many of which are 
under the impression they are buying e-bikes for their children when they are in fact, buying e-
motos, which do not fit the definition of an e-bike.  Councilor Barlow also stressed the 
importance of BPD stepping in to deter behavior to the extent they can.    
Councilor Carpenter stated she urged a constituent to report a recent encounter to the police, but 
that the constituent was reluctant to do so because they were not confident in the police response 
and wonders what BPD does with reports of e-moto incidents when they come in.  Councilor 
Carpenter questioned if there are any changes that need to be made at the ordinance level and is 
looking to BPD and DPW to provide input on that.  Councilor Carpenter also suggested that a 
committee or group be created through resolution to organize a citywide educational campaign.   
Chair Bergman expressed that the Committee needs to look at the bike ordinance to add e-motos 
and also look at sidewalk rules.  Chair Bergman added the role of e-moto sellers is worth 
considering and agrees with looking at enforcement and that the whole community needs to be 
engaged.   
Director Lewis summarized BPRW’s response to e-motos on the bike path and put up signs in 
various locations along bikepath.  Some of those signs have gone missing.  The department is 
creating permanent signs that specify no e-motos or motorcycles.  The department also did some 
outreach with the school, and Director Lewis said the school had a substantial campaign at the 
end of the year and believes e-moto traffic on the bike path has gone down.  Director Lewis also 
noted staff have collected data that shows e-motos account for 0.2% of bike path users.  Director 
Lewis clarified that when an incident occurs, the department tries to document it and provide that 
information to law enforcement and urges community members to do the same through either 
SeeClickFix or BPD’s non-emergency number.   
Councilor Barlow commented on how e-motos should be defined so signs prohibiting them are 
clear to the public.
Councilor Carpenter asked Director Lewis how to take a community education campaign for e-
motos to the next level.  Director Lewis offered BPRW support in educating the public and said 
Local Motion has held community meetings to discuss e-motos.  Director Lewis added the 
department has checked for alignment in the City’s ordinances with state laws and would be 
willing to participate in a multi-stakeholder educational group or initiative.   
Chair Bergman asked Director Lewis to state what resources BPRW has and if civil enforcement 
parks officials can be added and what money there is for enforcement and education efforts.  
Sharon Bushor commented BPRW’s signs could have pictures to address language barriers and 
stressed regulating e-motos is also a university and employer issue and that Local Motion is not a 
large enough platform to broadly educate the public and believes CATMA may have a role to 
play.   Bushor suggested BPRW and BPD create a shared budget to put toward education and 
enforcement.   
Councilor Grant commented that the issue seems to be enforcement and that the school personnel 
may have a role to play in intervening when underage students ride e-motos to school.   
Councilor Carpenter agreed with Councilor Grant’s comments and suggested the Committee ask 
the Mayor to appoint someone to be a coordinator of the initiatives discussed.  Councilor 
Carpenter also noted the nuisance e-moto riding behavior is not isolated to the bike path but an 
issue on city streets.     
Chair Bergman requested Polly Vanderputten relay the Committee’s desire to develop an 
approach to this issue with the coordination with the school district to the School Board.  
Vanderputten confirmed they would be in touch with Chairperson Wool and Superintendent 
Flanagan and would also email the Committee further ideas and comments.  
Chair Bergman invited City Engineer Laura Wheelock to speak from the DPW perspective on 
the issue, who summarized the following:  
• DPW currently has no ordinance changes in the works and that work done earlier in the 
year clarified city ordinances and brought them in alignment with state statutes, but noted 
the language at the state level is weak and suggested communities band together to 
change the language at that level.  
• DPW expects an ordinance or policy change will need to occur but that a public 
community conversation needs to happen first, pointing out e-motos are a form of 
alternate transportation, of which increasing the use of is an initiative of the City’s and 
would be in line with the BTV Mobility plan, which is being updated and why DPW has 
not proposed anything as of yet. 
• Past changes were developed in collaboration with the Walk/Bike Council and Local 
Motion who have more recommendations and would be a starting point for community 
input. 
• DPW fully supports stronger guidance and has already seen a difference from BPRW’s 
signage and the campaign last spring.
• Implementing speed limits on the bike path could be effective because it would apply to 
all modes of transportation and address issues with unsafe speeds in congested areas.   
• The Committee should consider if this is the right forum to take up this issue at this time 
and that there are challenges with enforcing ordinances against this behavior.   
City Engineer Wheelock clarified for Councilor Barlow that DPW is open to looking at imposing 
a speed limit or changing the age limit for bike path use but has concerns for vulnerable riders.  
Councilor Barlow agreed the conversation needs to be broadened outside the Committee and 
wants to hear from the school district and BPD on the issue.   
Richard Hillyard commented witnessing children as young as 7 or 8 riding to school on e-
scooters with no helmets and emphasized helmet safety needs to be part of the education.  
Hillyard also said at least some of the kids source the e-motos online and trade within the 
community.   
Sharon Bushor spoke to City Engineer Wheelock’s point about who should take lead on this 
issue and said whoever does take lead needs to have a clear, cohesive approach in tackling it.  
Bushor also stated the Walk/Bike Council does not focus enough on the pedestrian compared to 
riders.   
The Committee discussed next steps: 
• Councilor Carpenter said the Committee should go to the Mayor to assign a coordinator 
for the City and how that should be handled, and the Committee can continue to be 
involved but not lead.   
• Councilor Barlow supported Councilor Carpenter’s idea to authorize Chair Bergman to 
speak to the Mayor.   
• Chair Bergman noted there are many stakeholders and many parties information needs to 
be gathered from before change is made.  Chair Bergman requested that each committee 
member write individual requests for information and collective requests and 
recommendations, based on this meeting’s deliberations, to be considered at a future 
meeting, with the idea that the Committee get to a point of reaching a decision or motion 
on a proposal from the Committee.      
• Chair Bergman requested the City Attorney’s Office work provide input where needed 
and that the Committee needs to compile the ideas that have come out of 3 meetings on 
this topic.   
Councilor Grant said this topic is relevant to public safety and that the Public Safety Committee 
should take it on.    
5. Any Other Committee Business 
The Committee said they would meet again on the September 17, but will generate and circulate 
their lists by September 2 to committee members, key departments, and the Mayor.  
6. Adjournment
Motion to adjourn by Councilor Bergman, without objection. 
The meeting was adjourned at 6:10 PM.
